best.empty: Waiting for the first calculated site…

planner.dataNote: Data: JPL Horizons (DE441), airless, terrain horizon from LOLA. Each cell is the share of a {{days}}-day mission starting on that date.
planner.dataNoteBeginner: The greener the cell, the better the launch date for a {{days}}-day mission at that site. The Sun and Earth positions come from NASA data.

criteria.title: Suitability criteria
criteria.note: Project assumptions, not NASA requirements. They apply to the scenario, the comparison and the planner.

minSunElevation.label: Min. Sun elevation, °
minSunElevation.hint: The Sun counts as lit only above this angle over the terrain horizon. Grazing light gives little power.

minEarthElevation.label: Min. Earth elevation, °
minEarthElevation.hint: The Earth counts as visible only above this angle over the terrain horizon.

minWindowHours.label: Min. continuous window, h
minWindowHours.hint: Periods with both Sun and Earth that are shorter than this are not counted. 0 — count everything.

maxBlackoutHours.label: Max. darkness, h (0 — no limit)
maxBlackoutHours.hint: The longest period without the Sun that the lander survives on its battery. A mission with a longer darkness is not viable. Applies to the scenario and the comparison, not to the planner.

viablePercent.label: “Viable” from, %
viablePercent.hint: Share of the mission with power and communication from which the site is viable.

marginalPercent.label: “Marginal” from, %
marginalPercent.hint: Share of the mission from which the site is marginal; below it the site is not viable.

hints.sunlight: Share of the mission when the Sun is above the local horizon. No sunlight means solar panels produce nothing and the lander gets cold.
hints.earthLink: Share of the mission when Earth is visible from the site, so the lander can talk to Mission Control directly by radio.
hints.window: Share of the mission when there is both sunlight for power and a direct link to Earth. This is the best time to operate.
hints.longestDarkness: The longest continuous stretch without sunlight. The battery has to last that long.
hints.longestCommsGap: The longest continuous stretch when Earth is hidden and there is no direct radio contact.
hints.sunlightDuration: Total time the Sun is above the horizon during the mission.
hints.earthWindow: Total time Earth is visible and a direct radio link is possible.
hints.heatmap: Rows are landing sites, columns are launch dates. A greener cell means more sunlight and radio contact with Earth during the mission.
